title: Seqlocks and Snapshots
summary: Publishing a state that changes constantly, such as a game's player positions for an external tool - why readers can see torn data, double buffering, and the seqlock - a sequence counter that lets readers detect a write in progress and retry without ever blocking the writer.

cards.a: A read that sees part of an old state and part of a new one, a combination that never existed.

cards.q: What does an odd sequence counter tell a seqlock reader?
cards.a: A write is in progress, so it must try again.

cards.q: Why does the reader read the counter a second time after copying?
cards.a: If it changed, a write happened during the copy and the copy may be torn.

cards.q: Why is a seqlock better than a mutex for a game publishing state to a tool?
cards.a: The writer never waits for readers, so a slow or stalled tool cannot slow the game.
